records.gloss: And from the violet and the purple and the scarlet of crimson they made garments of woven work for serving in the holy [place]; and they made the garments of holiness which [are] for Aaron, as had commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: Out of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, finely woven garments were made for service in the holy place. Aaron's holy garments were made as well, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.1: And from the blue and the purple and the scarlet [yarn] they made woven garments for serving in the holy [place]; and they made the garments of holiness which [were] for Aaron, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.1: The workers used blue, purple and red yarn to weave the special clothes worn for serving in the holy place. They made the holy clothes for Aaron, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: they made the holy garments: the garments of chapter 28 are made
decisions.reason: Verses 1-31 tell how the priestly garments described in 28:1-43 were made, in nearly the same words, now told as done. The order differs a little: the ephod, the breastpiece, the robe, and then the tunics, turban, caps, undergarments and sash, ending with the gold plate. The workers are the skilled men and women led by Bezalel and Oholiab (35:30-36:2).

decisions.choice: woven garments: the priests' finely worked clothing
decisions.reason: See the note at 31:10. The phrase that follows, "for serving in the holy place", says what these garments were for.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh had commanded Moses: the refrain of the chapter
decisions.reason: These words close seven sections of verses 1-31 (verses 1, 5, 7, 21, 26, 29, 31): the garments as a whole, the band of the ephod, the onyx stones, the breastpiece, the robe, the linen garments and sash, and the plate on the turban. Each part is marked as made exactly as God had commanded. Nothing in the clothing is the workers' own design; all follows the pattern God gave Moses on the mountain (25:9, 40). The refrain comes again in the summary (verses 32, 42, 43) and through chapter 40 as the tabernacle is set up.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had commanded Moses
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded the same way at every level and in every verse, so that the reader hears the repetition (m3). The past perfect shows that the command came before the work.

decisions.choice: were made (Balanced); The workers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they". Balanced uses the passive and Readable names the workers, the craftsmen of 35:30-36:2. Readable says "red" for "scarlet", as in 28:5.

decisions.choice: was finished: the end of the work, as at creation

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of the tent of meeting: one structure

decisions.reason: The doubled phrase stresses that nothing was left out or changed. The same words are said of Noah building the ark (Genesis 6:22) and of Israel keeping the Passover (12:28, 50).

R.42: Every part of the work was done the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did it all.

decisions.choice: all the work: the labor of building
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in verse 32, labor or service. Verse 43 uses another word for "work", the one used of God's work in Genesis 2:2-3.

decisions.choice: according to all ... so they did: obedience stressed
decisions.reason: The verse puts the command first and repeats the summary of verse 32, framing the list of verses 33-41: everything brought to Moses was made as commanded.

records.source: וַיַּ֨רְא מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־כָּל־הַמְּלָאכָ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ עָשׂ֣וּ אֹתָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה כֵּ֣ן עָשׂ֑וּ וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֹתָ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And saw Moses all the work, and look, they had done it; as had commanded Yahweh, so they had done; and blessed them Moses.
pieces: Moses looked at all the work, and there it was, done in every point as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded. And Moses blessed them.

L.43: And Moses saw all the work, and look, they had done it; as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded, so they had done. And Moses blessed them.

R.43: Moses looked over all the work. Everything had been made the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded. Then Moses blessed the people.

decisions.choice: saw all the work, and look ... finished ... blessed: an echo of the end of creation
decisions.reason: The words recall Genesis 1:31-2:3. There God saw all that he had made, "and look, it was very good"; the heavens and the earth were finished; God finished the work he had done, and he blessed the seventh day. Here the work of the tabernacle is finished (verse 32), Moses sees all the work, "and look", it has been done, and he blesses. The word for "work" in this verse is the one used of God's work in Genesis 2:2-3. The text does not state the comparison; it lies in the shared words. They present the tabernacle, where God will live among his people (25:8), as a new beginning like the world God made, and the repeated "as Yahweh had commanded" as the obedient answer to God's word.

decisions.choice: Moses blessed them: the people who did the work
decisions.reason: "Them" is the Israelites who did the work. The words of the blessing are not given. Moses blesses the people again at the end of his life (Deuteronomy 33:1), and Aaron and the priests are given words to bless them with (Numbers 6:22-27).

decisions.choice: and look, they had done it: what Moses found
decisions.reason: "Look" turns to what Moses saw as he inspected: the work was complete and matched the command.

decisions.choice: there it was (Balanced); not rendered (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "look". Balanced says "there it was" and Readable states the result plainly.

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Readable names whom Moses blessed (m2).
